paper_metadata.title: Quantum Computational Algorithms for Derivative Pricing and Credit Risk in a Regime Switching Economy

summary: The paper presents four gate-based quantum finance experiments: a two-state Markov-chain state-preparation benchmark (T = 3, 6, 12, 24; N = 64; S = 1028), a static credit-risk VaR circuit, a regime-switching derivative-pricing circuit with 6 time steps and 128 shots, and a practical dynamic portfolio IQAE example with 3 and 6 time steps. Reported results are MSE-based and show simulator and small-QPU demonstrations only; the paper does not establish practical quantum advantage.

experiments.description: Gate-based quantum Markov-chain state preparation and evaluation of a two-state T-period regime-switching process, benchmarked on simulator and IBM Brisbane hardware.

algorithm.variant: Two-state discrete-time Markov chain state-preparation circuit with RY rotations and controlled rotations
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Steady-state initialization via RY(theta0) from transition probabilities

problem_formulation.encoding_details: One qubit per time step plus one initial qubit; amplitudes encode Markov-chain state probabilities via RY and controlled RY rotations
problem_formulation.objective_function: Prepare the exact discrete-time Markov-chain distribution over T periods and estimate its probability mass function; MSE against true probabilities

problem_instance.description: Two-state regime-switching Markov chain for good/bad economy states using NBER business-cycle transition probabilities and synthetic alternatives
problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Transition probabilities estimated from NBER expansion/recession counts; steady-state initialization used
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Mean-squared error over N=64 repetitions with S=1028 shots; evaluated on ibmq qasm simulator and ibm brisbane quantum processor

noise_model.noise_type: hardware noise on real QPU plus readout-error mitigation

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Transition probabilities derived from NBER chronology; steady-state probabilities used to initialize the chain
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Histogram-based probability estimation and MSE computation against exact probabilities

speedup_claims.caveats: This benchmark evaluates Markov-chain state-preparation accuracy; no classical baseline or speedup claim is reported.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(T) circuit depth for T time steps; state space size grows as 2^(T+1)

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: One qubit per time step plus one initial qubit; tested at T = 3, 6, 12, 24 with N = 64 and S = 1028 shots
limiting_factors: No classical baseline for speedup comparison
Task is state-preparation / distribution estimation, not an advantage benchmark
Hardware results are small-scale and MSE-focused

notes: Hardware includes both ibmq qasm simulator and ibm brisbane quantum processor; simulator type inferred as simulator_noisy because the paper reports a qasm simulator and real hardware runs, but does not specify a noise model for the simulator.
Number of qubits is not explicitly stated; inferred from the circuit description as one qubit per time step plus the initial qubit, i.e., T+1.
No asymptotic speedup claim is quantified for this Markov-chain state-preparation benchmark.
Paper reports MSE values on simulator and IBM Brisbane, but does not claim practical quantum advantage.

experiments.description: Static portfolio credit-risk estimation with and without regime switching, benchmarked on simulator and IBM Kolkata hardware.

algorithm.variant: Quantum risk analysis / credit-risk Value-at-Risk estimation with regime-switching state-dependent default probabilities
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Default probabilities and sensitivities set from Table 2; Markov-state-dependent U operator constructed from GE/BE parameters

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Default events encoded by Y-rotations on obligor qubits; normal-distribution register, weighted-sum register, and comparator used to estimate VaR confidence level
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate alpha = P(L <= x) for portfolio loss L and infer VaR by binary search
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Comparator flips objective qubit when total loss exceeds threshold; no explicit penalty formulation

problem_instance.description: Homogeneous static credit portfolio with one or two regime-switching economic states; VaR estimation for a portfolio of risky assets

dataset_specification.description: 1986-present transition probabilities used for regime switching; synthetic transition probabilities also tested

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Transition probabilities estimated from NBER expansion/recession counts; one-month default probability obtained by dividing the six-month approximation by T
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: MSE reported for simulator and quantum processor runs; exact classical benchmark used for comparison

noise_model.noise_type: hardware noise; readout mitigation and circuit optimization used

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classical computation of transition probabilities, normal-distribution discretization, and Taylor approximation of rotation angles
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Binary search over loss threshold L to infer VaR from estimated alpha

speedup_claims.conditions: for amplitude estimation-based VaR estimation and binary search over the loss threshold
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states the quadratic speedup in estimation error scaling, but the reported experiment is an accuracy benchmark rather than a direct runtime comparison.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(log n) binary search for VaR once alpha(L) can be estimated; amplitude estimation gives quadratic improvement over Monte Carlo
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(n) for classical Monte Carlo estimation of alpha; O(log n) binary search for VaR threshold search

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Amplitude-estimation-based VaR estimation with simulator and IBM Kolkata runs; exact qubit count not stated
limiting_factors: No reported end-to-end runtime advantage over classical methods
Circuit described as large and implemented with mitigation/optimization

notes: The paper reports the use of a qasm simulator and the ibm kolkata Falcon quantum processor; hardware type is therefore real_qpu_superconducting for the QPU run.
Exact qubit count is not explicitly stated for the full static-portfolio circuit; the paper describes registers MC, Z, X, S, and obj but does not give a total.
The paper frames the method as a quantum risk analysis circuit and reports MSE, but does not demonstrate practical advantage.

experiments.description: Derivative-pricing circuit for European call options without regime switching, benchmarked on simulator and IBM Sherbrooke hardware.

algorithm.variant: Quantum option pricing with QFT-based price evolution and linear amplitude payoff function
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Classical parameterization from Table 4; Brownian-motion and price registers initialized in computational basis

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Brownian-motion register B and price register P; QFT/iQFT used to evolve log-price; payoff encoded with linear amplitude function and comparator against strike register
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate European call price C(t,T,K,Xt,St)=E*[exp(-∫ r ds)(ST-K)+ | Ft]
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Comparator and controlled Pauli-polynomial rotation implement the payoff threshold

problem_instance.description: European-style option pricing under a regime-switching economy; this experiment is the no-switching baseline

dataset_specification.description: Single-asset option pricing with constant r and sigma; strike prices varied over five values

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Log-price evolution simulated in Fourier basis; payoff scaled for small-angle approximation
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: MSE against exact classical solution; S=128, B=5, N=100

noise_model.noise_type: hardware noise; PEC mentioned for hardware runs

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classical computation of log-price increments and scaling constant for payoff approximation
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Convert measured payoff probability to option price using the stated affine rescaling formula

speedup_claims.conditions: amplitude estimation for option pricing; estimation error scales as O(M^-1) versus O(M^-1/2)
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports the asymptotic scaling claim, not a direct empirical speedup measurement.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Amplitude estimation gives O(M^-1) estimation error versus classical Monte Carlo O(M^-1/2)

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: QAE/IQAE derivative-pricing circuit with 6 time steps, S = 128 shots, B = 5, N = 100; evaluated on simulator and IBM Sherbrooke
limiting_factors: No classical runtime comparison showing advantage
Authors explicitly note the circuit is prohibitively large for canonical QAE on current processors
Only small problem sizes and MSE reported

notes: The paper reports the ibmq simulator mps and ibm sherbrooke Eagle quantum processor; the QPU run is a real superconducting device.
The total qubit count is not explicitly stated; inferred from the described registers B, P, Str, Obj, and MC, but the exact total is not given.
The paper discusses theoretical quadratic improvement from QAE but does not demonstrate practical advantage.

experiments.description: Regime-switching derivative-pricing circuit for European call options, benchmarked on simulator and IBM Sherbrooke hardware.

algorithm.variant: Quantum option pricing with Markov-chain regime switching and four controlled price-update branches
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Classical parameterization from Table 4; Markov-chain state register added to control regime-dependent price updates

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Adds a Markov-chain register to the no-switching option-pricing circuit; four multi-controlled D gates cover all combinations of economy state and Brownian-motion direction
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate regime-switching European call price under state-dependent r and sigma
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Comparator and controlled payoff rotation as in the no-switching case

problem_instance.description: European-style option pricing in a two-state regime-switching economy

dataset_specification.description: 1986-present transition probabilities used for the regime-switching case

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: State-dependent interest rate and volatility parameters taken from Table 4; log-price increments controlled by regime and Brownian motion
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: MSE against exact classical solution; S=128, B=5, N=100

noise_model.noise_type: hardware noise; PEC mentioned for hardware runs

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classical computation of regime-dependent parameters and scaling constant
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Convert measured payoff probability to option price using the stated affine rescaling formula

speedup_claims.conditions: amplitude estimation for option pricing with regime switching; estimation error scales as O(M^-1) versus O(M^-1/2)
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports the asymptotic scaling claim, not a direct empirical speedup measurement.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Amplitude estimation gives O(M^-1) estimation error versus classical Monte Carlo O(M^-1/2)

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Iterative QAE for a dynamic portfolio example; Table 7 reports 3 and 6 time steps with ideal complexity 1082 and 12932 two-qubit gates and overhead about 2.0x and 1.88x
limiting_factors: Only simulator results reported for the practical example
No demonstrated end-to-end advantage over classical Monte Carlo

notes: The paper reports the ibmq simulator mps and ibm sherbrooke Eagle quantum processor; the QPU run is a real superconducting device.
The total qubit count is not explicitly stated; inferred from the described registers B, P, Str, Obj, and MC, but the exact total is not given.
The paper explicitly states the circuit is prohibitively large for canonical QAE and that the practical example is a proof of concept.

experiments.description: Practical dynamic-portfolio credit-risk estimation using iterative amplitude estimation on a simulator.

algorithm.variant: Iterative Quantum Amplitude Estimation (IQAE) for dynamic portfolio VaR
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Classical mean-variance portfolio weights computed from NBER expansion/recession statistics; Markov-chain state used to select weights

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Markov-chain register controls addition of relative growth rg to a growth register G; QAE maps probability of G<0 to alpha
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate alpha = P(L' <= 0) for a dynamic portfolio loss threshold and infer VaR
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Two’s-complement sign qubit used as objective bit; no explicit penalty terms

problem_instance.description: Dynamic portfolio of Aaa and Baa bonds with regime-dependent mean-variance weights
problem_instance.dataset_name: NBER business cycle chronology; FRED AAA10Y and BAA10Y series

dataset_specification.description: Aaa and Baa monthly series from 1986 to end of 2022; expansion/recession statistics used to compute regime parameters

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Compute means, standard deviations, and correlations separately for NBER expansions and recessions; derive stationary Markov transition probabilities and portfolio weights; map L' = L - Lmax
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: IQAE run on ibmq qasm simulator; Table 7 reports ideal alpha, estimate, confidence interval, and ideal complexity for 3 and 6 time steps

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classical mean-variance optimization and growth/loss remapping before quantum estimation
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Convert estimated alpha to VaR threshold; compare against ideal alpha and confidence interval

speedup_claims.conditions: Iterative amplitude estimation for dynamic portfolio VaR; asymptotic estimation error O(M^-1) versus O(M^-1/2)
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports asymptotic scaling and circuit complexity, not a direct runtime speedup on hardware.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: IQAE provides O(M^-1) estimation error; practical circuit complexity reported as ideal two-qubit-gate counts 1082 (3 steps) and 12932 (6 steps)
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Classical Monte Carlo error scales as O(M^-1/2)

notes: The paper states the practical example was evaluated on the ibmq qasm simulator; this is an ideal simulator, so hardware.type is simulator_other.
The exact qubit count is not explicitly stated; the paper mentions a growth register G, a Markov-chain register, and the IQAE setup with 4 evaluation qubits, but not the total circuit width.
